resources.string: Recognizes English, German, Spanish and French as you speak.
Choose the language you’ll speak. Uses more memory and may take longer.
Your selected language · On your phone
Turn your voice into written text, wherever you type.
Dictation stays on your phone. No account or subscription. Download once, then use it offline.
Microphone access is needed for dictation. Sprich always stops when you hide the keyboard or leave the text field.
Microphone access is off. Allow it here, or open Android app settings.
Sprich works as a keyboard so your words can appear in other apps. Use the keyboard button to switch back whenever you like.
Android shows a standard warning when you enable any keyboard. Sprich does not store your dictation audio or collect what you type.
Automatic covers all four languages. You can add Accurate later in Settings.
Sprich listens as soon as its keyboard opens. Pause to write; tap the bar to finish.
Tap the voice bar to speak. Pause to write; tap again to finish.

Your voice is processed on your phone. Ordinary dictation audio and text are not saved by Sprich. Words you explicitly teach are saved as text in your personal vocabulary. Text you insert belongs to the app you are using.
Internet access is used for speech downloads and personal APIs you choose to enable. No Sprich account, analytics or ads.
Starts listening as soon as Sprich appears. On by default; turn it off if you prefer to tap.
A short vibration for keyboard actions.
Say “new line” or “delete that”. Deletion only affects your last unchanged dictation.

Short swipe left: delete a word or symbol.
Long or slow swipe left: delete the last phrase. Hold at the end to keep deleting sentences; release to stop.
Swipe right: toggle whisper mode.
Swipe up out of the bar: typing keyboard.
Swipe down: stop listening and hide.
Hold still for 2½ seconds: Sprich settings.
After deleting, tap Undo to restore the last deletion.
For a quiet voice close to your phone. Swipe right on the bar to toggle.
Could not change whisper mode. Try again.
Release to delete · Move back to cancel
Release to delete · Hold to keep deleting
Release to stop listening and hide
Moving the cursor or changing a selection stops listening and cancels words that have not been inserted.
Automatic: Whisper Tiny language detection and FastConformer CTC. Accurate: Canary 180M Flash. All run on your phone.

Choose English, German, French or Spanish for Sprich.
Natural punctuation, fewer fillers, and clear self-corrections. Your meaning stays yours.
Speak naturally. An optional API turns your dictation into clear written text. Recognition can stay on your phone.
Voice recognition with your own API key. Local dictation stays available.
Names and words, written your way
No Sprich account, subscription, ads or analytics. Personal APIs are optional.

When you enable a personal API, audio or text goes directly to that provider. Sprich has no server in between. The provider’s prices and data policies apply. Your keys are encrypted on this phone and excluded from backups.
The people and projects behind Sprich
Sprich is built with the work of many people. Explore the software and speech models below, with their original licenses and notices. Everything here is available offline.

Cleanup sends your transcript and relevant vocabulary directly to %1$s. A connection check sends a short sample sentence. API charges may apply.
The check sends four seconds from your microphone to %1$s. Voice typing sends each phrase. Provider costs and data policies apply.
Your key is encrypted on this phone. Sprich keeps no dictation history.
This API stays off until you choose to use it.
Let %1$s see up to 512 characters before the cursor for spelling and continuity. Off initially. Excludes passwords and fields marked private.
Use on device if the API fails
Only when the speech files for your chosen mode are ready. Never switches to another API.
Share up to 100 saved terms with your voice provider to help recognize names. Cleanup already receives only terms in the transcript.

Optional hints for recognition. Leave these unselected to follow your dictation language.

Add A, B and similar labels when Meta can match them to the finished words. Labels start fresh with each phrase and do not identify people. Keeps Meta’s final wording; cleanup and spoken editing are skipped.

You can keep speaking · Tap to finish
Names, places, terms you use every day. Say a word three times, then show Sprich how to write it.
Corrections apply from your next dictation. Learned words use the voice mode you taught them in. Tap a word to review or remove it.
Say the same word or short phrase once per recording, in your usual voice. Sprich listens for up to four seconds.
Recognition stays on this phone. No writing cleanup or dictionary hints. Audio is discarded after each attempt; text is saved only when you choose Save word.

Recordings go directly to your enabled voice API. Its charges and data policy apply. No writing cleanup or dictionary hints. Sprich discards audio after each attempt; text is saved only when you choose Save word.
Allow microphone access to record a word.
Type the exact spelling, including capitals, or choose a name already on this phone.
Choose a name from this phone
Android shows the list. Sprich receives only the name you choose and saves nothing until you tap Save word.
Could not read that name. Type it instead or try again.
No compatible picker is available. Type the name instead.
Choose the forms that should become this word. Repeated results are suggested; you decide what to keep.
A selected form will be replaced whenever this voice mode returns it, including in other sentences. Select ordinary words with care.
No forms selected. Only the spelling will be saved, for vocabulary hints if you enable them.
Saves your spelling, the text Sprich heard and your selected corrections on this phone. No audio is saved. This does not train the speech model.
Saved in your personal vocabulary. Your selected corrections apply from your next dictation in this voice mode.
These recordings have not been saved. Leaving discards their text.
Could not open your voice settings. Go back and try again.
Download your selected voice mode on the Home screen, then return to teach a word.
No usable word came back. Try again with just the word or a short phrase.
Could not recognize this attempt. Try again; earlier attempts are still here.
Recording stopped. Your completed attempts are still here.
One of these forms already has another spelling. Deselect it or remove the earlier correction first.
This word is already saved for this voice mode. Remove the earlier entry to teach it again.
The Sprich application. Third-party code and speech models keep their own licenses.
Android user interface, accessibility, navigation, preferences and lifecycle components.
Android interface components and Material icons.
Asynchronous result interfaces used by Android libraries.
HTTPS connections for model downloads and optional personal APIs. Includes Public Suffix List data under MPL 2.0; its upstream source is https://publicsuffix.org/list/public_suffix_list.dat.
Encoding utilities used by archive handling.
Reading and writing structured application data.

Java APIs used on older Android versions. The Classpath exception permits linking independent modules under their own licenses. Unmodified upstream sources, including the build files, are available at the source link. See licenses/README.md in the Sprich repository for distribution requirements.
Runs speech recognition on the phone. Sprich builds the recognition-only Android runtime; unused speech synthesis and diarization are disabled.
Executes speech models locally. The upstream third-party notice bundle is retained in full; it also describes components used by other upstream platforms.
Finite-state tools used by the speech runtime.
Finite-state algorithms used by the speech runtime.
Structured data support inside the speech runtime.
Linear algebra inside the speech runtime. Unmodified corresponding sources are available from the source link.
Frequency analysis inside the speech runtime.
Native C++ support used by Sprich and its dependencies. The complete notice distributed with the exact Android NDK toolchain is included.
Identifies the language for Automatic mode. Downloaded separately; not included in the APK.
Recognition model for Automatic mode. Downloaded separately; not included in the APK. Its model card specifies NGC terms, not the Apache license of the training or conversion code.
Recognition model for Accurate mode. Downloaded separately; not included in the APK.
Detects when speech begins and ends. This small model is included in Sprich and runs locally. The exact model asset is pinned in docs/MODELS.md in the Sprich repository.
